summary: The note describes USB flash drives and their compatibility. They use the USB mass storage device class, which modern operating systems such as Windows, Linux, macOS and other Unix-like systems support natively, as well as many BIOS boot ROMs. USB 2.0 drives can hold more data and transfer faster than much larger optical discs such as CD-RW or DVD-RW, and many other devices can read them, including game consoles, DVD players, car entertainment systems and handheld devices, though SD cards are better suited to handhelds.
one_line: Overview of USB flash drives, their native OS support, and their compatibility with consoles, players and handheld devices.
key_facts: USB flash drives use the USB mass storage device class standard.
Modern operating systems such as Windows, Linux, macOS and other Unix-like systems support the USB mass storage device class natively.
Many BIOS boot ROMs support USB flash drives.
USB drives with USB 2.0 support can store more data than much larger optical disc drives like CD-RW or DVD-RW drives.
USB drives with USB 2.0 support can transfer data faster than much larger optical disc drives like CD-RW or DVD-RW drives.
USB flash drives can be read by the Xbox 360.
USB flash drives can be read by the PlayStation 3.
USB flash drives can be read by DVD players and automobile entertainment systems.
USB flash drives can be read by a number of handheld devices such as smartphones and tablet computers.
The electronically similar SD card is better suited for handheld devices than USB flash drives, according to the note.
